evidence: The back of the skull now visibly rests on the bench pad, and the upper back and torso remain supported. The earlier lifted-head failure is corrected.
Both arms extend upward from the shoulders, holding one continuous light straight bar with stable visible grips. This is a usable ordinary high starting pose; a pre-flexed low pose is not necessary.

Orange surfaces occupy the posterior upper-arm/triceps regions rather than the forearms. The head, bar, shoulders and elbows are all visible, with space for the forearms to fold toward a position above the forehead.
limitations: Single exact still inspected visually; it does not demonstrate any motion or guarantee future elbow-only articulation.
Feet and lower legs are outside this close upper-body framing. Human acceptance and trainer review remain separate.

animationGuidance.cycleDefinition: High reference pose → elbows flex to lower the bar to a comfortable position above the forehead, clear of the face → identical high reference pose.
animationGuidance.timing: Hold high 0–1 s; lower by elbow flexion 1–3.5 s; hold low 3.5–4.5 s; extend elbows 4.5–7 s; hold high 7–8 s.
mustPreserve: Head and upper back stay on the bench.
Upper arms remain elevated and nearly stationary; the forearms rotate around the elbows rather than lowering the upper arms into a bench press.
Bar remains one rigid object with fixed hand grips and stays clear of the face.
Orange posterior triceps surfaces persist throughout.
